title: Play Moves
unlocks: A game two people can actually play.
objective: Read moves from the keyboard, put X and O on the board in turn, and keep going until the board is full. Still one file, still no classes, still compiled by hand.
checks: A scripted sequence of moves lands on the right cells.
Players alternate: X, then O, then X.
The program exits when input runs out (EOF) instead of looping forever.
hints: You now have at least two jobs in one file: showing the board, and changing the board. Those are different things. What would you call each one if it were a function?

The player types 1 to 9 because that is how humans count squares. Your array runs 0 to 8. Do that subtraction in exactly ONE place, in a function with a name, rather than sprinkling -1 through your code.

while read a number from cin:
    index = number - 1
    place the current player's mark at index
    switch the current player
    print the board

`while (std::cin >> n)` is the loop condition you want. It is false when input runs out, which is what makes `printf '1
5
9
' | ./game` finish instead of spinning forever. If you use `while (true)` with a `cin >> n` inside, a piped test will hang the moment input ends.

prompts.title: My program hangs or loops forever
prompts.body:
My tic-tac-toe program either never stops or stops immediately when I pipe input into it:

    printf '1\n5\n9\n' | ./game

Here is my code:
<PASTE main.cpp>

Ask me what I expected to happen first. Then help me reason about what std::cin does when there is no more input, and how my loop condition responds to that. Do not paste corrected code at me.

prompts.title: Review my approach, don't write it
prompts.body:
I have just split my tic-tac-toe program into functions for the first time.

Here is my code:
<PASTE main.cpp>

Ask me questions about the split. Specifically: does each function do exactly one thing, could I explain what each one returns without looking, and is there anywhere I convert between the player's 1-9 and my 0-8 more than once? Do not rewrite it.

prompts.title: Quiz me on functions and input
prompts.body:
Quiz me on C++ functions, parameters, return values, and reading input with std::cin.

One question at a time, wait for my answer. Include at least one question about what happens when std::cin fails, and one where I have to say what a function returns without running it. If I am wrong, ask a smaller question rather than explaining.
